subject: CIs for session-specific population estimates from "derived" function OpenCR

messages.author: b97acb36e359be28
messages.subject: CIs for session-specific population estimates from "derived" function OpenCR
parts:
Hello, as the subject suggests, I am hoping to get confidence intervals around session-specific population estimates output from the "derived" function used on a openCR.fit model object.

I attempted to follow the workaround suggested by Dr. Efford in the vignette, which reads as follows: "(i) infer the point estimates with derived, (ii) assemble a start vector on the link scale(s) for an equivalent full-likelihood openCR.fit model that includes the derived abundances, and (iii) run openCR.fit with method = "none" to compute the hessian at the MLE, and hence the full variance-covariance matrix."

I can get to the last step, but I only see a superN parameter in the model results. I imagine I need to do something to get from this superN variance-covariance matrix to compute session-specific CIs, but lack the experience to know what this is. Also, the CIs I was hoping to compute are around session-specific population size estimates that were computed with the "HTbysession=TRUE" option in the "derived" function. Does this change the necessary steps to get CIs?

Thanks very much for any insight anyone can grant me. I can post code and/or data if needed.

Best,
Thomas

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: CIs for session-specific population estimates from "derived" function OpenCR
parts:
Hi
I don't think HTbysession changes anything. Have you thought of using a model specified in terms of session-specific N at the last stage (i.e. type = 'JSSAN')? I think that should work but I haven't tried it.
Murray
